title: Greedy selection and the optimization objective are separate decisions
problem: Choose independent additive reference groups under an equal-cost cardinality budget while protecting the weakest observed direction.
failure: Greedy maximization of minimum eigenvalue can have arbitrarily small approximation ratio even with strictly positive definite groups. Switching to log determinant restores a known greedy guarantee for that objective, but even exact determinant maximization can give arbitrarily poor weakest-direction performance.
correction: Specify the intended objective and resource constraints before selecting algorithms. Test against exhaustive small-instance optima. Use the classical monotone submodular guarantee only for normalized log determinant with independent PSD increments and SPD baseline. Retain the counterexamples for E selection and D/E objective mismatch.
transfer: Evaluate complementary sources jointly rather than relying on isolated rankings. A performance guarantee for one metric does not imply a guarantee for a different metric; check objective alignment and measurement independence.
limits: Equal-cost groups, independent additive PSD information, SPD baseline I. Unbounded counterexample uses unbounded group extent. 2300 diagonal triples, 405 exact determinant-ratio comparisons, five finite-k checks. No unequal-cost, correlated-noise, physical, organizational, novelty or independent validation claim.
author: TOTO
